title: Alpine a110 tasarımı Paris Otomobil Fuarı'nda sergilenecek
summary: Fransız spor otomobil markası Alpine, yenilenen elektrikli A110 modelinin tasarımını önizleyen bire bir ölçekli heykelini ekim ayında Paris'te sergileyecek.
body:
Alpine, yenilenen Alpine A110 modelinin tasarımını gözler önüne seren bire bir ölçekli bir heykeli ekim ayında düzenlenecek Paris Otomobil Fuarı'nda sergilemeye hazırlanıyor. Carscoops'un aktardığına göre, gelecek yıl yollara çıkması planlanan yeni elektrikli coupe modelinin hatlarını gizemli bir örtü altında sergileyecek olan bu özel heykel, markanın fuardaki standının odak noktası olacak. 

## Tasarım ve batarya düzeni

Yeni modelin hatları klasik A110 ruhunu korurken, mevcut kasaya kıyasla daha uzun, ince ve süper otomobil benzeri bir duruş sergiliyor. Tasarımında süpersonik yolcu uçağı Concorde'dan ilham alan araç, zemin döşemesini alçak tutmak için tabana tek büyük bir batarya yerleştirmek yerine şasinin iki ucuna konumlandırılan iki küçük batarya düzeniyle gelecek. Bu yapı sayesinde yüzde 40'a 60 ön-arka ağırlık dağılımı hedeflenirken, 800 voltluk elektrik sistemi hızlı şarj desteği sunacak. 

## Hibrit motor ihtimali ve ABD pazarı

Her ne kadar araç öncelikli olarak tamamen elektrikli olarak tasarlandıysa da, markanın CEO'su Philippe Krief platformun içten yanmalı motorlara da uyum sağlayabilecek şekilde geliştirildiğini belirtti. Şirket, hibrit motor seçenekleri konusunda henüz kesin kararını vermezken, benzinli motor seçeneğinin ABD pazarında satışa çıkabilmek adına kritik önem taşıdığı ifade ediliyor.

**Neden önemli?** Elektrikli spor otomobil pazarına yönelik beklentileri şekillendiren yeni Alpine A110, hem yenilikçi batarya yerleşimiyle mühendislik açısından dikkat çekiyor hem de olası içten yanmalı motor seçenekleriyle otomobil tutkunlarının taleplerine açık kapı bırakıyor.

sources.title: Alpine Teases Next A110’s Design, But It’s What’s Underneath That Will Make Or Break It

source_texts.title: Alpine Teases Next A110’s Design, But It’s What’s Underneath That Will Make Or Break It
source_texts.summary: French sports car is going electric and Alpine’s full-size sculpture reveals the two-seater’s evolved design
source_texts.text:
- Alpine will show a 1:1 sculpture of the new A110 at this October’s Paris Motor Show.
- Design is recognisable as an A110, but looks longer, leaner and more supercar-like.
- A110 will debut in 2027 as an EV but Alpine hints that hybrid engines will fit chassis.
Beautiful cars are sometimes likened to sculptures, but French sports car brand Alpine’s latest concept really is a sculpture. The full scale exhibit previews the look of next year’s new Alpine A110 and will be the focal point of the brand’s Paris Motor Show stand this October.
The sculpture reveals the design of the 2028 A110 without revealing too much, if that makes sense. It’s as if someone has dropped a silk sheet over the coupe’s bodywork, then pulled the air out from underneath it. What you see is the shape and contours of the aluminium skin and a hint at some of the details, while still leaving some mystery.
Related: Americans Might Force Alpine To Put Gas Back In Its New Electric Sports Car
Alpine says the tension visible in the blue veil is meant to look like it was caught by the wind, a nod to lightness and aerodynamics. It even claims one of the big inspirations was Concorde, the supersonic passenger jet co-created by Britain and Frances.
But that doesn’t mean Alpine has junked everything we loved about the outgoing A110, itself heavily inspired by the classic 1960s original. The V-shaped nose and dual light setup are still there, and though the sculpture tells us the new car will be leaner and possibly lower and longer, you’re not going to mistake it for anything else.
Design Evolution, Powertrain Revolution
Unless you’ve got your eyes closed when one drives past, in which case you might assume it was a runaway washing machine. Because the A110 is going electric. At the Goodwood Festival of Speed in July Alpine demo’d the new hardware in stretched version of the current A110 (below) called the A110 Future. That hardware includes a dual-motor rear axle with active torque vectoring and clever wheel-slip control. Today’s A110 is lauded for its agility, but the EV is shaping up to be even more mobile.
It’ll also have an unusual battery arrangement. Instead of having one massive battery under the floor of the APP platform, the new A110 will have two smaller batteries placed at each end of the chassis. That keeps the floorpan low and the driving position and roof, too. It will also help Alpine achieve a 40:60 front to rear weight distribution. An 800-volt electric system will ensure fast charging, though the exact speed and range figures are still secret. As is the weight, which is expected to balloon by 660 lbs (300 kg).
Electric First, Possible ICE Option Later
Also secret are Alpine’s intentions when it comes to combustion power. The A110 was conceived as an EV when it looked like electric cars were set to make gas ones a minority in short order. But while EV sales continue to grow in Europe, where they now account for one in four new cars, enthusiast buyers have signalled their preference for petrol engines. And it sounds like Alpine is listening.
“Before you ask, yes the platform is designed to accommodate an internal combustion engine,” Alpine’s CEO Philippe Krief told British magazine Autocar in March. At Goodwood, four months later, he said a decision over whether to make a petrol model will be made by the end of 2026. If it gets the green light it could take around two years to reach production.
Could Come To America
Although Krief gave no indication of which ICE motor might find its way into the A110’s chassis, there is one obvious source. Horse Powertrain, the company created by Alpine’s parent company Renault and China’s Geely, has developed multiple hybrid engines, one of which is good for 349 hp (354 PS) and 380 lb-ft (515 Nm).
A combustion engine option would be essential if Alpine ever wanted to bring the A110 to the US – where the current car was never available, and where EV sales are very weak. Expansion to America was previously baked into Alpine’s growth plans, but they were put on hold in 2025, in part due to the introduction of tariffs by President Trump. But Krief revealed this summer that the A110 was being put through US crash tests.
